critical_insights.description: Distinguish external consistency or serialization order from preservation of specified application invariants; the papers can address different correctness questions without contradiction.
Explain that TrueTime exposes bounded clock uncertainty and supports timestamp-ordering rules, but does not replace replication agreement or transaction coordination.

Explain that Calvin places transaction-sequence agreement before execution and uses deterministic locking to shorten distributed transactions' contention footprints, while sequencing and replication still have costs.
Account for Calvin's need to determine transaction read/write sets before execution and to handle nondeterministic results explicitly when applying it to this service.
State that coordination avoidance is conditional on invariant confluence for a particular set of operations, merge behavior and invariants, rather than universal for transfers or stock decrements.
Keep throughput, tail latency and partition-time availability distinct; note that Calvin's stated high-availability usage is not CAP availability.
critical_insights.evidence: Paper-2 page 1 footnote 1 and section 6; Paper-1 and Paper-3 evaluation discussions

critical_insights.description: Require the distinguishing experiment to hold the required correctness guarantee, workload definition and resource budget fixed across mechanisms.
critical_insights.evidence: Task-level experimental-design requirement; the supplied papers do not provide a controlled three-way comparison

critical_insights.description: Vary contention, cross-partition transaction ratio and network conditions so the experiment can expose mechanism-specific costs instead of reporting one aggregate throughput number.
critical_insights.evidence: Task-level experiment inferred from Paper-1 wide-area costs, Paper-2 contention analysis and Paper-3 coordination costs

critical_insights.description: Use an explicit correctness oracle and state competing predictions whose outcomes distinguish preordering/contention-footprint effects from safe coordination avoidance or weaker guarantees.
critical_insights.evidence: Task-level discriminating-test requirement grounded in the distinct mechanisms of Paper-1, Paper-2 and Paper-3

critical_insights.description: Identify the unresolved service question as which invariant and transaction classes are safely coordination-free, and under what workload or network regime the remaining coordination becomes the bottleneck.
critical_insights.evidence: Synthesis across Paper-1, Paper-2 and Paper-3; explicitly a task-level inference, not a published head-to-head result

catastrophic_risks.description: Treating bounded clock uncertainty as perfect clocks or assuming TrueTime alone replaces agreement.
Allowing arbitrary stock decrements or transfers to merge without validating the relevant invariants, risking oversell or conservation failure.
Claiming that the papers directly prove a universal performance winner or equivalent guarantees across all partitions and workloads.
catastrophic_risks.evidence: The papers use different system models and evaluations; Paper-2 page 1 footnote 1 explicitly distinguishes availability terminology

competing_solutions: Coordinate all relevant multi-record operations under a sufficiently strong transaction guarantee, accepting its cost.
Use deterministic preordering for known transaction footprints and explicitly account for sequencing, planning and replication costs.
Partition transaction classes by proven invariant-confluence conditions, coordinating only classes that need it; validate hybrid boundary semantics.
high_value_insights: Distinguish moving coordination outside lock-holding intervals from removing the semantic need for coordination.
Use a correctness-matched factorial microbenchmark to distinguish contention-footprint effects from safely coordination-free operation or weaker-guarantee effects.
success_criteria: Explains the apparent conflict without inventing contradictory experimental results or equating unlike correctness guarantees.
Grounds at least two mechanisms in accurate paper claims and clearly labels the service-specific hidden assumption and inference.
Proposes a feasible experiment with competing predictions, safety oracle, controls and a falsification outcome; no catastrophic unsafe claim.
